The speculations of the 1930s made real:: The speculations of the 1930s made real: Greece, Turkey and Cyprus under one republican administration, the strait and the islands one customs water.
The basin as one state: Brazil, Colombia: The basin as one state: Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia administering the forest, its rivers and its peoples together.
The sea as a shared interior: Turkey, Ro: The sea as a shared interior: Turkey, Romania, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Georgia and Moldova in one customs and security union with free movement across the water.
The Sahel as one state: Mali, Burkina Fa: The Sahel as one state: Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Mauritania and Chad under a shared military and civil administration, holding the ground the empires of the river once held.
Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti as one fe: Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti as one federation around the strait: one port authority, one highland market, one voice on the Red Sea.
Pilsudski's old proposal made real: the: Pilsudski's old proposal made real: the lands between the seas - Poland, the Baltics, Belarus and Ukraine, with the Danube powers welcome - as one federation that neither Berlin nor Moscow may order about.
Pan-Slavism carried to its end: every st: Pan-Slavism carried to its end: every state where a Slavic people governs, from the Elbe to the Pacific, one union of the related - not a restoration of anyone's empire, and written so in its charter.
The community of the Spanish-speaking pe: The community of the Spanish-speaking peoples as one federal state: Spain and the republics of the Americas in a union of equal members, the ocean a domestic sea rather than a distance.
The Sahrawi national liberation movement: The Sahrawi national liberation movement founded in 1973, proclaiming the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic in 1976 and holding the territory east of the berm since the 1991 ceasefire. Morocco administers the rest and proposes autonomy under its sovereignty; the front insists the question is decolonisation, not autonomy, and the referendum it was promised has simply never been held.
The political umbrella that the M23 move: The political umbrella that the M23 movement formed with allied groups in 2023, administering captured towns in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo while saying it fights a war against a state that never honoured its own peace deals. Kinshasa, the United Nations and a panel of experts say the movement is armed and directed from across the Rwandan border; Kigali says it is defending its own security.
The southern Yemeni movement formed in 2: The southern Yemeni movement formed in 2017, gathering the Hirak that wants South Yemen back as an independent state on its 1990 borders. It is a partner in Saudi-backed government coalitions and their rival at the same time: administers Aden, fields forces paid by the coalition, and keeps the flag of the south flying over both.
The anglophone Cameroonians' movement, b: The anglophone Cameroonians' movement, born of 2016 lawyer and teacher protests against the imposition of French in courts and schools, declaring independence of the former British Southern Cameroons a year later. The separatist camp is divided among rival administrations and armed self-defence groups; the state's answer has been a curfew, burned villages and a war almost nobody outside the region names.
The organised independence movement of C: The organised independence movement of Catalonia as it acts in the open: the assemblies, the annual demonstration that fills the city on the Diada, the parties and associations that turned a question of statute reform into a question of a republic. Its referendum of 2017 was illegal under the Spanish constitution and binding for a generation of its voters at the same time.
The Kanak independence movement of New C: The Kanak independence movement of New Caledonia, heir of the FLNKS: three referendums against French sovereignty, two won by staying, the third boycotted after the elder statesmen asked for a mourning year and were refused. The 2024 riots burned what the ballot did not settle, and the question of who may vote - and who was never asked - is again the whole question.
The Rohingya armed group whose attacks o: The Rohingya armed group whose attacks on police posts in northern Rakhine in 2016 and 2017 were answered by a military campaign that drove more than 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. Myanmar's government declared it a terrorist organisation, and it has had little armed presence inside the country since, working from the refugee camps and the diaspora.
Colombia's oldest guerrilla, founded in: Colombia's oldest guerrilla, founded in 1964 and, since the FARC demobilised, its largest. It is in negotiations with the government of Gustavo Petro under a ceasefire that has been renewed and broken, and it lives off kidnapping, extortion and the drug trade in Arauca, Norte de Santander, Cauca and Choco. Colombia, the United States and the European Union list it as a terrorist organisation.
The armed wing of the United Liberation: The armed wing of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua, which took over from the older Free Papua Movement. It attacks Indonesian soldiers, police and workers at the Grasberg mine, mostly in the highlands of Papua and West Papua provinces, and Indonesia classifies it as a separatist and terrorist organisation. Its political wing is heard more in Pacific capitals, where the Melanesian Spearhead Group and several states receive it, than in the highlands themselves.
The faith the state declares and the peo: The faith the state declares and the people it declares itself of. A declaration needs the group to live in the country in a share large enough to carry the name; declaring a secular state needs nobody's permission. A declaration against the majority costs the country's calm.
